source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

lines.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.
lines.zh: 哈囉，這裡是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。我是 Neil。

lines.en: And I'm Pippa.
lines.zh: 我是 Pippa。

lines.en: When it comes to household chores, jobs like cleaning, washing clothes or looking after the kids, it's often women who do most of the work.
lines.zh: 說到家務——像是打掃、洗衣服或照顧小孩這些工作——通常都是女性做了大部分。

lines.en: Here, two female listeners of BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World share their experiences.
lines.zh: 這裡有兩位 BBC 世界廣播節目《People Fixing the World》的女性聽眾分享她們的經驗。

lines.en: Do they sound familiar to you?
lines.zh: 你聽起來覺得熟悉嗎？

lines.en: I do everything. I do all the house chores, I do the food shopping, I do all the cooking, I clean the bathroom.
lines.zh: 所有事都是我在做。所有家事是我做、買菜是我、煮飯全是我、浴室也是我在洗。

lines.en: Are the chores done equally between me and my husband?
lines.zh: 家事是我和我先生平均分擔的嗎？

lines.en: No, they're not done equally.
lines.zh: 不，並沒有平均分擔。

lines.en: I do most of the chores.
lines.zh: 大部分家事都是我在做。

lines.en: So, you're a family man, Neil.
lines.zh: Neil，你是有家庭的人。

lines.en: Do you do your fair share of household chores?
lines.zh: 你有分擔你應做的那份家事嗎？

lines.en: I think so.
lines.zh: 我想有吧。

lines.en: My wife works part time and I work full time, so when I'm not working, I do things, and when she's not working, she does things.
lines.zh: 我太太做兼職，我做全職，所以我不上班的時候就做家事，她不上班的時候就換她做。

lines.en: Yeah, it's similar in my house, so me and my husband try to split things, but it's difficult, isn't it?
lines.zh: 對，我家也差不多，我和我先生會試著分工，但這很難，對吧？

lines.en: It is.
lines.zh: 確實很難。

lines.en: Of course, no one enjoys cleaning the toilet or taking out the bins, but there is a serious side to the issue.
lines.zh: 當然，沒有人喜歡洗馬桶或倒垃圾，但這個議題也有嚴肅的一面。

lines.en: Figures from UN Women, an organisation promoting gender equality, suggest that every day women around the world spend three hours more than men on unpaid care and domestic work.
lines.zh: 推動性別平等的組織「聯合國婦女署」的數據顯示，全世界的女性每天花在無償照護與家務上的時間比男性多三個小時。

lines.en: So, in this episode, we'll be hearing about two projects helping husbands and wives share the housework more fairly.
lines.zh: 所以在這一集，我們會聽到兩個幫助夫妻更公平分擔家事的計畫。

lines.en: And as usual, you'll find a quiz and a worksheet to go with this episode on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 一如往常，我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 上有這一集的測驗和學習單。

lines.en: But now I have a question for you, Pippa.
lines.zh: 不過現在，Pippa，我有個問題要問你。

lines.en: According to a survey conducted by Good Housekeeping magazine earlier this year, what is the most hated household chore in Britain?
lines.zh: 根據《Good Housekeeping》雜誌今年稍早做的調查，英國人最討厭的家事是哪一項？

lines.en: Is it: a) deep cleaning the oven, b) scrubbing the toilet, or c) cleaning the windows?
lines.zh: 是：a) 深層清潔烤箱、b) 刷馬桶，還是 c) 擦窗戶？

lines.en: Hmm. I'm going to say deep cleaning the oven because I really hate that job.
lines.zh: 嗯。我要選深層清潔烤箱，因為我真的很討厭那個工作。

lines.en: I hardly ever do it.
lines.zh: 我幾乎從來不做。

lines.en: I don't like any of those, but we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
lines.zh: 這些我都不喜歡，不過我們會在節目最後揭曉答案。

lines.en: Now, the first project we're going to look at is on the remote Indonesian island of Rote.
lines.zh: 我們要看的第一個計畫，位在印尼偏遠的羅特島。

lines.en: Here, men traditionally work as rice farmers or fishermen, while women look after the home, the children and older people.
lines.zh: 在那裡，男性傳統上是稻農或漁夫，女性則負責照顧家庭、小孩和長輩。

lines.en: But with few washing machines and no running water, these domestic chores take a long time.
lines.zh: 但因為洗衣機很少、又沒有自來水，這些家務要花很長的時間。

lines.en: The NGO ARUNGI runs a project trying to change attitudes about the role of the island's women.
lines.zh: 非政府組織 ARUNGI 推動一項計畫，試圖改變大家對島上女性角色的看法。

lines.en: They work alongside community leaders like Mama Shilpa, who spoke with BBC World Service reporter Ade Mardiyati.
lines.zh: 他們和社區領袖一起合作，例如 Shilpa 媽媽，她接受了 BBC 世界廣播記者 Ade Mardiyati 的訪問。

lines.en: It is expected that the tasks done in the house, like holding the child, feeding the child, washing dishes, cooking, will all be done by the mother.
lines.zh: 大家預期家裡的工作，像是抱小孩、餵小孩、洗碗、煮飯，全都由媽媽來做。

lines.en: Shilpa tells me these are all considered women's work.
lines.zh: Shilpa 告訴我，這些都被認為是「女人的工作」。

lines.en: And you might be thinking, Well, the man is busy in the fields, so it's just a fair division of labour.
lines.zh: 你可能會想：嗯，男人在田裡很忙，所以這只是公平的分工。

lines.en: But Shilpa tells me women also help out in the fields.
lines.zh: 但 Shilpa 告訴我，女人也會到田裡幫忙。

lines.en: On Rote, cleaning, cooking and sweeping are considered women's work – a negative term for boring and repetitive tasks which are traditionally done by women.
lines.zh: 在羅特島，打掃、煮飯和掃地都被認為是「女人的工作」——這是一個負面的說法，指傳統上由女性做的無聊、重複性工作。

lines.en: Many cultures have a division of labour – a way of organising work where different tasks are done by different groups of people.
lines.zh: 許多文化都有分工——一種讓不同群體的人做不同工作的組織方式。

lines.en: But on Rote this means women work even harder, helping out with the farming and fishing too.
lines.zh: 但在羅特島，這代表女性要做得更辛苦，還得幫忙務農和捕魚。

lines.en: You might think this only happens in traditional societies, but research suggests that women in wealthy countries also spend much more time on unpaid care work than men.
lines.zh: 你可能以為這只會發生在傳統社會，但研究顯示，富裕國家的女性花在無償照護工作上的時間也遠比男性多。

lines.en: One such country is Croatia, where the NGO Status M run their Superdads project.
lines.zh: 克羅埃西亞就是這樣的國家之一，非政府組織 Status M 在那裡推動「超級爸爸」計畫。

lines.en: Project worker Anamarija Soča leads workshops encouraging dads and sons to take some of the pressure off mums.
lines.zh: 計畫工作人員 Anamarija Soča 帶領工作坊，鼓勵爸爸和兒子幫媽媽分擔一些壓力。

lines.en: Here, she explains the benefits of this to the BBC World Service.
lines.zh: 在這裡，她向 BBC 世界廣播說明這樣做的好處。

lines.en: Mothers have, you know, of course, more space for their careers, or hobbies, or just simply to rest – I mean, just to take a breather.
lines.zh: 媽媽們當然就有更多空間經營事業、發展興趣，或單純休息一下——我是說，喘口氣。

lines.en: Women tend to especially appreciate men who do these kinds of chores.
lines.zh: 女性通常特別感激會做這類家事的男性。

lines.en: And when they start pulling their weight, then they jokingly say that, yeah, women tend to nag less.
lines.zh: 而當男性開始盡自己的本分時，她們會開玩笑說，對啊，女人就比較不會嘮叨了。

lines.en: Sometimes mums need to take a breather – an informal way of saying stop and rest a while.
lines.zh: 有時候媽媽需要「take a breather」——這是「停下來休息一會兒」的非正式說法。

lines.en: Anamarija also thinks women appreciate it when their husbands pull their weight.
lines.zh: Anamarija 也認為，先生盡到自己的本分時，太太會很感激。

lines.en: If you pull your weight, you work as hard as everyone else.
lines.zh: 如果你「pull your weight」，就是你和其他人一樣努力。

lines.en: Both these NGO projects agree about one thing – men doing more to help around the house results in happier homes, even if that means cleaning the toilet now and then.
lines.zh: 這兩個非政府組織的計畫都認同一件事——男性多幫忙家事，家庭會更快樂，即使這代表偶爾要洗馬桶。

lines.en: And speaking of cleaning the toilet, what was the answer to your quiz question, Neil?
lines.zh: 說到洗馬桶，Neil，你的問題答案是什麼？

lines.en: I asked you what chore is the most hated in Britain.
lines.zh: 我問你英國人最討厭的家事是哪一項。

lines.en: I thought it was cleaning the oven.
lines.zh: 我以為是清烤箱。

lines.en: Well, I'm afraid that's not the right answer.
lines.zh: 嗯，很遺憾，這不是正確答案。

lines.en: People hate cleaning the windows even more than scrubbing the oven.
lines.zh: 大家討厭擦窗戶，甚至超過刷烤箱。

lines.en: Apparently, 23% of the people who did the survey said cleaning the windows.
lines.zh: 顯然有 23% 的受訪者選了擦窗戶。

lines.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with 'chores' – household tasks like cleaning, washing and ironing that have to be done regularly.
lines.zh: 好。我們來複習今天學到的詞彙，首先是「chores」——必須定期做的家務，像是打掃、洗衣和燙衣服。

lines.en: If you do your fair share of work, you do a reasonable amount.
lines.zh: 如果你做了自己應做的那份工作（your fair share），就是做了合理的份量。

lines.en: 'Women's work' is a negative term for the boring and repetitive tasks which are stereotypically done by women.
lines.zh: 「Women's work」是一個負面說法，指刻板印象中由女性做的無聊、重複性工作。

lines.en: The 'division of labour' is a way of organising work where different tasks are done by different groups of people.
lines.zh: 「division of labour」是一種組織工作的方式，讓不同群體的人做不同的工作。

lines.en: The idiom 'take a breather' means to stop what you're doing for a short time and rest.
lines.zh: 慣用語「take a breather」的意思是暫時停下手邊的事休息一下。

lines.en: And finally, if you pull your weight, you work as hard as everyone else doing the same job.
lines.zh: 最後，如果你「pull your weight」，就是你和其他做同樣工作的人一樣努力。

lines.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember, you can find a free transcript including all the vocabulary on our website, at bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 我們的六分鐘又到了，但別忘了，我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 上有包含所有詞彙的免費逐字稿。

lines.en: Goodbye for now.
lines.zh: 先說再見了。

lines.en: Goodbye!
lines.zh: 再見！
